architecture.mechanism: IoT-based real-time fire detection with automatic cooling activation triggered when temperature exceeds a predefined safety threshold of 45°C, using continuous monitoring to detect abnormal thermal conditions and reduce battery temperature.
architecture.intervention: Install LM35 temperature sensors and a flame detection unit on the 2020 Nissan Rogue battery pack (and in the cabin air intake path) with an Arduino-based controller that, upon detecting ≥45°C or flame signature, (1) activates active cooling of the battery module, (2) triggers a cabin positive-pressure ventilation / HVAC recirculation shutoff with HEPA-grade filtration to block smoke ingress, (3) automatically unlocks doors and powers window controls to preserve occupant egress, and (4) pushes an alert to the driver and first responders via cloud IoT dashboard within the 1.8-second detection window.
architecture.expected_effect: Thermal runaway propagation is suppressed by reducing battery temperature by 12–15°C within 90 seconds of cooling activation; smoke ingress into the cabin is blocked and egress paths (doors, windows) remain functional, giving occupants a safe evacuation window before the runaway progresses to the black-smoke stage observed in the complaint.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument a representative R519-class Li-ion battery pack with the LM35 + flame detector + Arduino Nano + cooling-fan loop and a cabin smoke-ingress mock-up; induce thermal runaway via nail penetration or overcharge, and measure (a) time-to-detection (must be ≤1.8 s), (b) battery temperature drop (must reach 12–15°C reduction within 90 s of activation), (c) cabin PM2.5/CO concentration during the event (must stay below ACUC/UL 2580 occupant-exposure limits), and (d) door-unlock and window-drop actuation latency (must complete before smoke opacity reaches the cabin). The mechanism is falsified if any of these four metrics fail their target under three repeated trials.
